standard_prerequisites.name: Suspension as a higher inductive type
standard_prerequisites.statement: The suspension susp(A) of a type A is generated by north, south : susp(A) and merid : prd{a:A} north = south, with the matching induction and recursion principles.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement is about susp(A) and the proof defines a family P on susp(A) x susp(A) by recursion on the two suspensions and checks the meridian condition (source lines 543-571).

standard_prerequisites.name: The sethood criterion for reflexive mere relations
standard_prerequisites.statement: If P is a reflexive mere relation on a type X and there is tau : prd{x,y:X} P(x,y) -> (x = y), then X is a set and P(x,y) is equivalent to (x = y) for all x, y; this is book Theorem 7.2.2.
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied twice, at source lines 573-575 to reduce the goal to constructing tau, and at line 610 to conclude sethood and the equivalence of P with the identity type. The criterion lies in another chapter file and is declared as a non-load-bearing source pointer.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mere propositions and the unit type
standard_prerequisites.statement: An inhabited mere proposition is contractible and hence equivalent, and therefore equal by univalence, to the unit type.
standard_prerequisites.use: Used in the meridian condition at source lines 563-569 to turn the four values of P into equal types, since the assumed inhabitant a : A makes A equivalent to unit.

core_obligations: Define P : susp(A) -> susp(A) -> type by P(north,north) := unit, P(north,south) := A, P(south,north) := A, P(south,south) := unit, check that the definition respects the meridian: for a : A the four values become equal because a inhabits A, so A is equivalent to unit and univalence turns the equivalences into identities (source lines 543-569).
Check that P(x,y) is a mere proposition for all x, y by induction on x and on y, using that being a mere proposition is itself a mere proposition (source lines 569-571).

Observe that P is reflexive, invoke the author's sethood criterion for reflexive mere relations, and reduce everything to the construction of tau : prd{x,y:susp(A)} P(x,y) -> (x = y) (source lines 573-575).

Build tau by double induction: tau(north,north,u) := refl, tau(north,south,a) := merid(a) and symmetrically tau(south,north,a) := opp(merid(a)), tau(south,south,u) := refl, then verify the two meridian transport conditions, the first by function extensionality from refl . merid(a) = merid(a) = merid(x) and the second by induction on the second argument (source lines 576-608).

Conclude from the criterion that susp(A) is a set and that P(x,y) is equivalent to the identity type, and instantiate x := north, y := south to obtain the equivalence A ~ (north = south) (source lines 610-611).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the family P on susp(A) x susp(A) and verify the meridian condition and mere-propositionality.
Apply the reflexive-relation sethood criterion and reduce to constructing tau.
Construct tau by double induction and check the two transport conditions along the meridian.
Conclude sethood of susp(A), the equivalence of P with the identity type, and the north-south case.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.13 at source lines 537-540: if A is a mere proposition then its suspension is a set and A is equivalent to the path space north = south. The 71-line proof is an encode-decode argument that has to be built from scratch: it defines a family P on susp(A) x susp(A) with values unit and A (lines 543-554), checks that this definition survives the meridian, which is where an inhabitant of A is used to make A equivalent to unit and univalence turns the equivalence into the needed identity (lines 555-569), and checks mere-propositionality of every P(x,y) by double induction (lines 569-571). Sethood is then obtained from the author's criterion for reflexive mere relations, so the rest of the proof is the construction of tau : prd{x,y} P(x,y) -> (x = y) by double induction together with the two transport conditions along the meridian, the first of which needs function extensionality and the computation refl . merid(a) = merid(a) (lines 576-608). The statement records neither P nor the transport conditions.
